bullets.text: Total PIF grew ~220,000 (+2.2%) from year-end 2006 and ~3% YOY; renewal policies represent 78% of private passenger auto book; retention and policy life metrics increased in almost every tier but trailed prior year.

Underwriting margin remained strong at 10.5%, even with higher mid-quarter storm frequency; current margin suggests some closure of the gap between the reaffirmed 4% underwriting profit target and recent double-digit margins.

Average auto premiums were reduced 2–4%, with wider and deeper ranges in selected segments; PGR expects a period-over-period deflationary effect, and measurable response to rating actions emerged late in the quarter.

Top-line results were the most disappointing for some time, and aggregate growth measures were slow; PGR adapted its primary performance measures to reflect an emphasis on unit growth in policies in force.

Results did not suggest highly notable changes in frequency or severity, outside of seasonality and rapidly rising New York PIP costs; multi-year frequency declines previously led the industry toward lower price levels.

Direct auto PIF grew ~5% YOY, responding to rate actions with higher conversion and early retention improvements; new auto applications grew in half of states, but Florida, Texas, and Virginia missed growth objectives.

Aired first TV commercials with a new ad agency promoting concierge claims, increasing consumer awareness; with over 50 centers, PGR expects to increase marketing focus and price attractiveness in those service areas.

Current market rate stability or reduction made price-cut reactions less dramatic; multi-year frequency declines led the industry to begin settling at lower prices, where PGR historically hesitated on downward adjustments fearing rate shock.

Direct customer shift toward online quoting and purchasing continued; expanded "e-fulfillment" paperless policy availability, and tested paper billing reduction offers that fund tree planting for each enrolled customer, which were well received.

Slower growth created focus on operational challenges; PGR evaluates growth versus margin trade-offs in selected segments and addressed structural impediments to customer rate expectations, believing retention will improve.
